title: Cloud/DevOps Engineer
description: A Cloud/DevOps Engineer builds and maintains the infrastructure and automation pipelines that let teams ship software reliably — writing Infrastructure-as-Code with tools like Terraform or Pulumi, containerizing services with Docker, and orchestrating deployments on Kubernetes. Day-to-day work includes building CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), setting up observability with metrics/logging/tracing stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK), and managing on-call incident response against SLOs/SLIs and error budgets.
certifications: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
demand_level: High and growing — platform-engineering roles inside Global Capability Centres are expanding at roughly 18% year-over-year as they build internal developer platforms rather than just maintaining infrastructure.
salary_range: India: ~₹4–9 LPA entry, ₹8–35 LPA mid, ₹18–60+ LPA senior/SRE/platform. Cloud certifications reliably add 20–35% to offers at 2–6 years of experience; staff/principal roles at top firms go well above this range.

title: Cybersecurity Engineer
description: A Cybersecurity Engineer secures systems against attack — running vulnerability assessments and penetration tests, configuring and tuning SIEM tools (Splunk, QRadar) to detect anomalous activity, and hardening infrastructure against common attack classes like SQL injection, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. Day-to-day work includes threat modeling new features before launch, investigating incidents by analyzing logs and malware samples, and implementing controls such as network segmentation, least-privilege IAM policies, and encryption key management.
demand_level: High and rising — driven by expanding digital-security investment across sectors plus new compliance work created by India's DPDP Act.
salary_range: India: ~₹3.5–7 LPA entry, ₹8–28 LPA mid, ₹18–50 LPA senior/architect. OSCP- and CISSP-holders and specialists (AppSec, cloud security, red team) trend toward the top of each band; CISO-level pay goes considerably higher still.

title: Blockchain Engineer
description: A Blockchain Engineer designs and builds decentralized applications and protocol-level infrastructure — writing and auditing smart contracts (commonly Solidity on EVM chains, or Rust on Solana), optimizing for gas efficiency, and reasoning about the security trade-offs of consensus mechanisms like proof-of-stake and BFT variants. Day-to-day work includes writing test suites to catch reentrancy and overflow vulnerabilities before deployment, integrating with node infrastructure and oracles, and monitoring contract behavior after mainnet launch.
demand_level: High but volatile — a smaller, far less standardized market than mainstream software roles. Reported hiring and salary figures vary widely across sources, more so than any other role in this set.
salary_range: India: roughly ₹5–11 LPA entry, ₹10–20 LPA mid, ₹20–30+ LPA senior/architect — treat as a rough guide only. This was the least consistent dataset found; one otherwise-credible source reported a ₹32.6L average, well above what most others show, and none of the sources agreed closely.

title: Robotics Engineer
description: A Robotics Engineer builds systems that sense, plan, and act in the physical world — implementing sensor fusion (combining IMU, LiDAR, and camera data via Kalman or particle filters), writing motion-planning and control algorithms (PID, MPC), and working within frameworks like ROS/ROS2 to coordinate perception, planning, and actuation nodes. Day-to-day work includes calibrating sensors, tuning controllers for stability under real-world noise, and testing in simulation (Gazebo, Isaac Sim) before deploying to physical hardware.
demand_level: Growing but smaller in absolute hiring volume than mainstream software roles — accelerating with Industry 4.0 adoption in manufacturing, logistics, and warehouse automation.
salary_range: India: ~₹4–6.5 LPA entry, ₹9–18 LPA mid, ₹18–24+ LPA senior. Software/perception-heavy specialists (computer vision, SLAM) trend toward the top of this band.

title: Game Developer
description: A Game Developer builds interactive experiences using engines like Unity or Unreal Engine — implementing gameplay systems (character state machines, physics interactions), optimizing rendering pipelines (draw calls, LOD, shader performance) to hit frame-rate targets, and scripting in C# or C++/Blueprints. Day-to-day work includes profiling for performance bottlenecks on target hardware, tuning game feel through iteration (hitboxes, input latency, animation blending), and working closely with artists and designers to implement levels and mechanics.
demand_level: Moderate — a smaller domestic market than mainstream IT roles, though mobile gaming and esports are expanding it. India pay for this title trails US/EU studio pay by a wide margin for the same work.
salary_range: India: ~₹3.5–6 LPA entry, ₹8–15 LPA mid, ₹15–22 LPA senior — notably below backend/frontend/ML pay at equivalent experience.

title: Data Engineer/Data Scientist
description: A Data Engineer/Data Scientist builds the pipelines that move and transform data at scale, then uses that data to answer questions and build models — writing ETL/ELT jobs with tools like Spark or Airflow, designing warehouse schemas (star/snowflake) for efficient querying, and running statistical analysis or building predictive models (regression, classification, clustering) to guide decisions. Day-to-day work includes optimizing SQL queries and pipeline runtimes for large datasets, validating data quality and lineage, and communicating findings through dashboards or A/B test results.
certifications: Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Engineer Associate
demand_level: Very high — industry hiring projections put India's additional data-professional requirement at 300,000+ by 2028.
salary_range: India: ~₹5–10 LPA entry, ₹12–32 LPA mid, ₹19–80 LPA senior/AI-specialized. The data-engineer/data-scientist distinction is blurring in practice, with GenAI/LLM-adjacent specialists earning the most.
